A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, algorithms, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 2 report original synthetic experiments comparing Noise and Fine-Tune unlearning with SGD retraining, averaged over 50 repetitions.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the synthetic experiments and adds original handwritten-digit experiments, reported in Figure 2b with settings in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the synthetic loss remain unchanged. Appendix B newly explains the existing L1 penalty and coordinate expansion; these are not newly introduced method components. The real-data experiment applies the retained approach under additional evaluation settings.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only constructed synthetic objectives. v2 retains these and adds handwritten-digit classification on the Digit dataset described as a subset of Alpaydin and Kaynak's dataset, substantially extending coverage to real data.

E2.justification: Both versions compare Noise and Fine-Tune with SGD retraining from scratch. The added digit experiment uses the same comparator, without adding another evaluated unlearning method.

E3.justification: The complexity-ratio and excess-risk-threshold evaluation design is retained. The added digit protocol uses L2-regularized cross-entropy, batches of 64, decaying SGD and the actual distance between optima for noise calibration. Appendix D specifies its 60-point parameter grids; these are settings for a new experiment.

E4.justification: v2 extends the privacy-versus-excess-risk sensitivity analysis to real data and compares its phase-boundary shape with the synthetic case in Section 5.4. This is a limited extension of the existing analysis; no controlled smoothness or component ablation is added.

E5.justification: The synthetic experiment retains 50 repetitions and averaging. The digit experiment follows the same 50-run averaging practice. Neither version reports experimental confidence intervals, significance tests or seed-specific variability.

E6.justification: Figure 2b adds an entire empirical complexity-ratio surface for handwritten digits, showing the three regimes and a different frontier shape from the synthetic case. The original synthetic heatmap is retained unchanged as Figure 2a. These are additional results under different conditions, not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 adds an inference about exact unlearning using an infinite privacy-strength parameter. Corollary 2 explicitly reexpresses the existing upper bound as a sufficient condition for achieving a ratio below any chosen gamma. The original assumptions, Theorems 1–3 and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the minimax complexity ratio, upper and lower bounds, three regimes and quadratic dependence on the forgetting fraction. Renaming the impossible regime to inefficient preserves its stated meaning: unlearning cannot asymptotically outperform retraining.

C2.justification: v2 discusses exact-unlearning applicability and exclusions, clarifies the algorithm dependence of the upper bound, and attributes the real-data frontier's shape to smoothness. Appendix B also explains the numerical motivation for the existing synthetic loss construction.

D1.justification: New Appendix D documents the digit experiment's regularization weight, grid ranges, batch size and learning-rate schedule, including initialization at 0.01 and multiplication by 0.6 every 1000 epochs. Conversely, v2 omits v1's explicit counts of 36 synthetic grid values, without establishing that those settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Alpaydin and Kaynak (1998) dataset reference and clarifies the framework's relationship to existing exact-unlearning approaches. The related-work survey and central novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 consistently changes impossible to inefficient, refines theorem labels and several explanations, separates synthetic and real-data experimental subsections, and adds acknowledgements and Appendix D. Most of the existing narrative is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 expands from a single-column synthetic plot to a full-width, two-panel synthetic/real-data display. Figure 1 changes its privacy-axis reference from 1/r_f to 1/(r_f sqrt(d)) and relabels the inefficient regime. Captions and running headers also change.

improvement.justification: The digit experiment adds useful evidence beyond v1's synthetic demonstration, while Appendix D and the corrected schematic improve documentation and precision. The gain is limited: the core theory is unchanged, the new experiment uses the true distance between optima for noise calibration, and explicit synthetic grid counts are lost.
